his_statement: Programme; foncteur D*; deux constructions
statement: For a base S on which p is locally nilpotent, a BT group has a finite locally free contravariant Dieudonné crystal, functorial under base change. After reduction to characteristic p it has F and V with FV=VF=p. The exponential/universal-extension and cohomological constructions must be compared; the manuscript only announces them. Under the crystalline nilpotent-reduction equivalence, the underlying crystal depends only on G modulo p; this does not identify the categories of BT groups before and after reduction without Hodge data.

his_statement: Ker F=Im V; filtration canonique
statement: The Hodge filtration is related to the kernel/image of F,V after reduction to the characteristic-p base, with a Frobenius twist. Over a perfect ring the twist is invertible and the filtration is recovered uniquely. Over a general base, exactness and local freeness for realizable Dieudonné crystals are additional assertions, not consequences of cancelling p alone. Codex43 explicitly asserts exactness and locally free subcrystals for every Dieudonné crystal, not just those already known to arise from a BT group.

his_statement: G_K n’a pas de ss-groupe isom. à G_a, puisque G_K admet un modèle de Néron
statement: If an algebraic group G_K over the fraction field of a nontrivial discrete valuation ring has a Néron lft-model, it has no K-subgroup isomorphic to Ga. Its derivative would put a nonzero tangent vector in every power of the uniformizer times the finite free Lie lattice, an impossibility. his_statement: Harvard, October27,1963
statement: For a reductive algebraic group over a field of characteristicp>0 and a fixed nonzero vector in a rational representation, a homogeneous invariant polynomial nonzero there exists, and it can be chosen in p-power degree. computation: root_computation_notes.md supplies the general coefficient argument; binom(p^r m,p^r)=m modp is nonzero. The result is attributed to Mumford’s preface and Haboush’s solution, not to a new Grothendieck conjecture.
fate: R-Q33: Haboush1975 establishes geometric reductivity. The exact invariant-polynomial formulation is read in Sastry–Seshadri2011, introductionp415. Taking the coefficient of t^(d−p^r) in F(x+tv), where d=p^r m and p∤m, converts any separating invariant to p-power degree; thus the source’s p-power condition introduces no remaining gap.
fate_date: Published1975; first circulation not established.
present_status: As of 19 November 2026: The positive-characteristic geometric-reductivity conjecture stated in Mumford’s preface asks that reductive algebraic groups be geometrically reductive.

his_statement: Harvard, October27,1963
statement: The literal claim that every finite group of isometries of a convex set in a semisimple flag building has a fixed point is false without an additional restriction excluding the subbuilding case.
computation: Take the entire rank-one spherical building SL2(C), whose points are P1(C) at mutual distanceπ. It is convex. The finite Q8 generated by diag(i,−i) and [[0,1],[−1,0]] acts isometrically; a fixed line must be one of the first matrix’s eigenlines, which the second exchanges. There is no fixed point. Independent b_tits_check.py verifies the matrix relations; root_computation_notes.md proves every hypothesis.
fate: R-Q33: Ramos-Cuevas2013 proves the modern centre theorem with a subbuilding alternative (C-SA04-695). The literal preface shorthand is refuted by the rank-one Q8 example; this is Mumford’s reused text, not a conjecture newly attributed to Grothendieck.

These open texts and the independent Kummer proof settle the usual setting and sufficiency; an exact primary proof including every singular/arbitrary-field convention of the manuscript was not located.

his_statement: extension universelle ... annulé par V
statement: Over a perfect field of characteristic p, for an abelian variety B, the extension 0→α_B→B^(p)→B→0 given by Verschiebung is universal among commutative extensions of B by affine commutative groups H with V_H=0, with the usual finite-type/fppf conventions.
computation: For any extension0→H→E→B→0, naturality makes V_E:E^(p)→E kill H^(p) when V_H=0. It descends to a lift u:B^(p)→E of V_B. Its restriction α_B→H gives the pushout presentation. Any two lifts differ by a map B^(p)→H, which is zero because an abelian variety has only constant maps to an affine group and a group map sends zero to zero. Thus the pushout map is unique.
fate: The precise universal formulation was searched using Verschiebung, affine Vkilled extensions, Cartier duality and universal vector extensions. Opened Chai–Oort2009 §10.24 supplies natural Verschiebung for flat commutative groups; Fonseca–Matthes2022 §2.2 supplies the neighboring vector-extension universal property and cites Mazur–Messing I.1.10. No opened primary source with this exact Vkilled-affine universal formulation was located. The above independent proof establishes the stated perfect-field finite-type interpretation; historical attribution remains unassigned.

present_status: As of 19 November 2026: Mathematically proved here for the explicitly stated commutative perfect-field category. The category and general-base extension require specification before promoting the source into a broader relative theorem.

his_statement: enveloppe vectorielle ... Lie(B*) dual
statement: Let A=B* and α_B=kerV_B. The universal vector extension of B is the pushout of its Verschiebung extension along the universal linear vector-group map α_B→V(Lie(A)^dual). The finite group whose vector envelope is used is α_B; its Cartier dual kerF_A has height one and supplies the Lie-space description.
computation: For a finite group α with Cartier dual β, primitives in O(α)=O(β)* identify with Lie(β). Hence Hom(α,Ga)=Lie(β)=Lie(A) here; more generally maps to vector groups are represented by Lie(A)^dual with linear maps between vector groups. Apply the universal pushout in C-SA04-707 to H=Ga^r (whose Verschiebung is zero). This gives the standard vector-extension universal property. A literal antecedent referring the vector envelope to β instead of α would be wrong: Hom(μ_p,Ga)=0.
fate: Opened Fonseca–Matthes2022 §2.2, pp2–3, verifies the usual universal vector extension and its Hom-to-Ext property, citing Mazur–Messing I.1.10. The α_B pushout derivation is independently supplied here, with the linearity convention explicit. The precise historical wording and antecedent are not certified from ink.
